title: Your first moves: three habits
outcomes: Takes space in the centre with a pawn on move one
Brings knights out toward the centre, and castles when the squares are clear
Knows these are habits with conditions: a threat or a concrete tactic can override them

steps.text: Early in a game your pieces start behind pawns. Three habits help: **1.** Put a pawn in the centre (e4 or d4) to give pieces room. **2.** Bring your knights and bishops out toward the middle (this is called **developing** them), each piece once. **3.** Castle early to tuck your king away. They are habits, not laws: a threat from your opponent comes first.

steps.caption: A pawn to e4 takes space in the centre. Black does the same.

line.say: The pawn takes space in the centre.
Black answers in the same way.

steps.title: Centre pawn, edge pawn
steps.prompt: In the second case White opened with the edge pawn a4 instead of e4. Predict first: can the bishop on f1 move?

steps.text: Pieces work best where they reach many squares. A knight in the middle of the board reaches up to eight squares; on the edge, at most four, and in a corner only two. So bring pieces toward the centre, and bring each new piece out rather than moving the same one again and again.

steps.caption: The knight on d4 reaches eight squares, the one on the h-file four, and the one in the corner two.

steps.title: Same knight, other square
steps.prompt: Both Nf3 and Nh3 bring the knight out. Predict first: do they work equally well?

steps.text: Your king is safest tucked behind its pawns in the corner, and castling also brings a rook toward the middle. Be careful with pawns in front of your king: every pawn move changes the shelter and leaves weak squares that enemy pieces can use. Here is how quickly that can go wrong.

steps.caption: After 1.f3 e5 2.g4, Black plays Qh4 and it is checkmate.

line.say: The queen gives check along the diagonal. White has no answer.

steps.prompt: Before you answered the last three questions: what did you check first, a threat against you, a piece to develop, or castling? Why that order?
